In accordance with the terms and conditions of the Grant Agreement between Global Fund and WAPCAS, the Grant can fund the procurement of male condoms through the UNOPS Procurement mechanism, with the Global Fund executing a direct disbursement from the Global Fund to UNOPS. Condoms will be delivered to the Ghana Health Service – National Aids Control Program (NACP).

The project's Legal Agreement, signed on the 2nd of November 2021 and ending on the 31st of July 2022 has an implementation and delivery timeline of 8 months and a total budget of USD 490,000.11 (Four hundred and Ninety Thousand United States Dollars and Eleven Cents).  The project has been extended to March 2023.

However, over time, the project implementation period has been amended and extended to March 2023 following approval for the reprogramming of project savings for the procurement of an extra 9,000 gross (1,296,000 units) in addition to the original request for 52,780 gross (7.6 million units), as well as a new request for 53,820 gross (7,750,000 units) on an additional budget of USD 352,084, bringing the total budget to USD 842,084
UNDP also procured medical equipment and related logistics for health facilities and CHPS compounds in Accra Metropolitan Area and Ga Central municipality to strengthen essential health service delivery. In addition, UNDP in partnership with Ghana Health Service constructed a CHPS compound in Chorkor to further strengthen primary health care in urban slum areas

projects.name: HIV prevention, treatment, care and support services
projects.description:
Linked to UBRAF outcome 1: People living with, at risk of and affected by HIV obtain equitable access and reap equitable benefits from HIV prevention, treatment, care and support services.

Country summary of results:
HIV prevention was prioritized by the joint programme in 2022. WHO and UNAIDS contributed to the publication of the revised policy guidelines for PrEP and HIV Self-testing. PrEP and PEP for all along with innovations such as Cabotegravir and the Dapivirine ring were included in the revision. Advocacy continued for condoms and lubricants for key and priority populations, and UNFPA supported the launch of a campaign to increase accessibility and use of condoms for HIV and STI prevention particularly for AGYW and key-priority populations. UNAIDS guided the HIV Prevention Acceleration Team supported by the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, to complete the HIV Prevention Self-Assessment Tool (PSAT) with AGYW. Findings suggested that there is a need for a costed, comprehensive, and tailored HIV prevention package of services for AGYW. Regarding HIV treatment, care, and support, DSD strategies were scaled across the country with technical support from the joint programme. UNICEF, WHO, and UNAIDS significantly contributed to the publication of the test, treat, and track Consolidated Guidelines for HIV Care in Ghana. The guideline closely aligns with 2022 WHO guidance on testing and treatment and was reviewed by WHO program experts in the Global Centre before publication. With advocacy from WHO Ghana, the guidelines included the adoption of the more efficacious and pediatric friendly anti-retroviral DTG-10 regime, and WHO supported a costed road map for DTG-10 transition for all. UNICEF led a study in the 5 highest burden regions to audit the care of 426 HIV exposed infants of which 189 were HIV positive. The study aim was to identify the factors contributing to new infant infections and develop context-specific interventions to eliminate MTCT and new postnatal infections. Regarding family-based testing, 179 PLHIVs were offered Family HIV Testing, 141 accepted and 309 children were tracked for testing. Among the children tracked, 284 were successfully contacted and 262 were tested for HIV. Of those tested, 53 were found positive and 46 (86.8%) of these children were linked to care. This pilot was meant to encourage accelerated scale up of family-based testing for all by the GF PRs. The joint programme supported capacity building to accelerate progress on the Global AIDS targets. UNESCO supported the Ministry of Education/Ghana Education Service, by building capacities of 4908 teachers on HIV Prevention Education in schools including schools for learners with disabilities. As a result, a total of about 43,000 learners continue to receive lessons on HIV prevention in schools through these trained teachers. Additionally, WHO provided technical support to build capacity and quality of DSD service delivery by providing access to an online training platform for health care workers (doctors, nurses, and pharmacists). The online course was completed by over 4000 health care workers who were awarded Continuous Professional Education credits. Finally, UNAIDS and WHO provided technical assistance to the Ghana AIDS Commisison and the National AIDS Control Programme to elaborate the GAM report, and the HIV Spectrum epidemic estimates. Also, technical advisory was provided to both entities to analyse information in the Situation Rooms.

projects.name: Communities and HIV resourced to lead HIV service delivery, advocate for and enjoy their right to health, and social and structural drivers
projects.description:
Linked to UBRAF Outcome 2: Communities of people living with, at risk of and affected by HIV, including key populations, women and young people, are empowered, enabled and effectively resourced to lead HIV service delivery, advocate for and enjoy their right to health, and social and structural drivers of the HIV epidemic are removed.

Country summary of results: (*Note; UNDP activities included here were separately reported by UNDP. Therefore, we will not include financial data for that UNDP-led activity in this sub-output). 
The joint programme works across the domains of the Global AIDS Strategy (GAS) to ensure that the HIV response in Ghana is people-centered and optimized for communities and networks of people living with, at risk of and affected by HIV, including key populations, women and young people. UNDP led a significant assessment on the structural drivers of stigma and discrimination in 10 of the largest health facilities in Greater Accra, the region with the highest burden of HIV in the country. The goal of the assessment was to strengthen stigma reduction efforts and ensure that health facilities and health care workers are equipped to provide nondiscriminatory services. UNDP in partnership with the NACP conducted health care worker baseline assessments, client stigma perception assessments, and capacity building trainings. As a result of findings of these assessments, 213 (162 women, 51 men) health workers in these 10 health facilities in Greater Accra Region have the requisite skills to provide non-discriminatory services to over 17,000 PLHIV. The population of PLHIV in Greater Accra includes all populations and is more likely to include AGYW networks and networks of PLHIV from KPs. Participants in the assessment, directors of the 10 health facilities, increased their knowledge, management of frontline healthcare workers to promote policies that eliminate stigma and discrimination, and capacities to champion policies and strategies, such as the National Human Rights Strategy to Eliminate Stigma and Discrimination, with the MOH, Ghana Health Service, and leadership in agencies such as the National Health Insurance Authority. The assessment resulted in a reduction of HIV related stigma and discrimination in 10 of the largest health facilities in Greater Accra and created health director champion advocates for the elimination of stigma and discrimination at HIV service delivery in the region with the highest HIV burden. Furthermore, in partnership with the Ghana AIDS Commission, UNDP provided capacity building to the leadership of the national and regional persons living with HIV (NAP+) to empower them to improve their skills in advocacy and knowledge sharing around the removal of social and structural barriers related to stigma and discrimination. The capacity building resulted in the championing of equitable access to HIV services from a people-centered, people-led human rights perspective. Community engagement and advocacy by the PLHIV were enhanced as they took greater leadership roles with the CCM and on national steering committees. As a result of the capacity building by UNDP and advocacy with Government partners, by UNAIDS and WHO, PLHIV played a more significant role in the implementation of the GF NFM III, particularly related to activities for AGYW and those lead by PLHIV community cadres to reduce new infections and ensure greater continuity of treatment and care by mothers and adolescents newly infected with HIV. UNAIDS and WHO served as technical leads on the steering committee of the CSO GF principal recipient and led advocacy for accountability around community engagement—always questioning the role of PLHIV, AGYW, and KPs in service delivery to ensure that the GAS is achieved with communities.
projects.outcome: Key and marginalized populations are empowered to access quality HIV/AIDS services

projects.name: HIV prevention, treatment, care and support services
projects.description:
Linked to UBRAF outcome 1: People living with, at risk of and affected by HIV obtain equitable access and reap equitable benefits from HIV prevention, treatment, care and support services.

Country summary of results:
HIV prevention was prioritized by the joint programme in 2022. WHO and UNAIDS contributed to the publication of the revised policy guidelines for PrEP and HIV Self-testing. PrEP and PEP for all along with innovations such as Cabotegravir and the Dapivirine ring were included in the revision. Advocacy continued for condoms and lubricants for key and priority populations, and UNFPA supported the launch of a campaign to increase accessibility and use of condoms for HIV and STI prevention particularly for AGYW and key-priority populations. UNAIDS guided the HIV Prevention Acceleration Team supported by the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, to complete the HIV Prevention Self-Assessment Tool (PSAT) with AGYW. Findings suggested that there is a need for a costed, comprehensive, and tailored HIV prevention package of services for AGYW. Regarding HIV treatment, care, and support, DSD strategies were scaled across the country with technical support from the joint programme. UNICEF, WHO, and UNAIDS significantly contributed to the publication of the test, treat, and track Consolidated Guidelines for HIV Care in Ghana. The guideline closely aligns with 2022 WHO guidance on testing and treatment and was reviewed by WHO program experts in the Global Centre before publication. With advocacy from WHO Ghana, the guidelines included the adoption of the more efficacious and pediatric friendly anti-retroviral DTG-10 regime, and WHO supported a costed road map for DTG-10 transition for all. UNICEF led a study in the 5 highest burden regions to audit the care of 426 HIV exposed infants of which 189 were HIV positive. The study aim was to identify the factors contributing to new infant infections and develop context-specific interventions to eliminate MTCT and new postnatal infections. Regarding family-based testing, 179 PLHIVs were offered Family HIV Testing, 141 accepted and 309 children were tracked for testing. Among the children tracked, 284 were successfully contacted and 262 were tested for HIV. Of those tested, 53 were found positive and 46 (86.8%) of these children were linked to care. This pilot was meant to encourage accelerated scale up of family-based testing for all by the GF PRs. The joint programme supported capacity building to accelerate progress on the Global AIDS targets. UNESCO supported the Ministry of Education/Ghana Education Service, by building capacities of 4908 teachers on HIV Prevention Education in schools including schools for learners with disabilities. As a result, a total of about 43,000 learners continue to receive lessons on HIV prevention in schools through these trained teachers. Additionally, WHO provided technical support to build capacity and quality of DSD service delivery by providing access to an online training platform for health care workers (doctors, nurses, and pharmacists). The online course was completed by over 4000 health care workers who were awarded Continuous Professional Education credits. Finally, UNAIDS and WHO provided technical assistance to the Ghana AIDS Commisison and the National AIDS Control Programme to elaborate the GAM report, and the HIV Spectrum epidemic estimates. Also, technical advisory was provided to both entities to analyse information in the Situation Rooms.

projects.name: Communities and HIV resourced to lead HIV service delivery, advocate for and enjoy their right to health, and social and structural drivers
projects.description:
Linked to UBRAF Outcome 2: Communities of people living with, at risk of and affected by HIV, including key populations, women and young people, are empowered, enabled and effectively resourced to lead HIV service delivery, advocate for and enjoy their right to health, and social and structural drivers of the HIV epidemic are removed.

Country summary of results: (*Note; UNDP activities included here were separately reported by UNDP. Therefore, we will not include financial data for that UNDP-led activity in this sub-output). 
The joint programme works across the domains of the Global AIDS Strategy (GAS) to ensure that the HIV response in Ghana is people-centered and optimized for communities and networks of people living with, at risk of and affected by HIV, including key populations, women and young people. UNDP led a significant assessment on the structural drivers of stigma and discrimination in 10 of the largest health facilities in Greater Accra, the region with the highest burden of HIV in the country. The goal of the assessment was to strengthen stigma reduction efforts and ensure that health facilities and health care workers are equipped to provide nondiscriminatory services. UNDP in partnership with the NACP conducted health care worker baseline assessments, client stigma perception assessments, and capacity building trainings. As a result of findings of these assessments, 213 (162 women, 51 men) health workers in these 10 health facilities in Greater Accra Region have the requisite skills to provide non-discriminatory services to over 17,000 PLHIV. The population of PLHIV in Greater Accra includes all populations and is more likely to include AGYW networks and networks of PLHIV from KPs. Participants in the assessment, directors of the 10 health facilities, increased their knowledge, management of frontline healthcare workers to promote policies that eliminate stigma and discrimination, and capacities to champion policies and strategies, such as the National Human Rights Strategy to Eliminate Stigma and Discrimination, with the MOH, Ghana Health Service, and leadership in agencies such as the National Health Insurance Authority. The assessment resulted in a reduction of HIV related stigma and discrimination in 10 of the largest health facilities in Greater Accra and created health director champion advocates for the elimination of stigma and discrimination at HIV service delivery in the region with the highest HIV burden. Furthermore, in partnership with the Ghana AIDS Commission, UNDP provided capacity building to the leadership of the national and regional persons living with HIV (NAP+) to empower them to improve their skills in advocacy and knowledge sharing around the removal of social and structural barriers related to stigma and discrimination. The capacity building resulted in the championing of equitable access to HIV services from a people-centered, people-led human rights perspective. Community engagement and advocacy by the PLHIV were enhanced as they took greater leadership roles with the CCM and on national steering committees. As a result of the capacity building by UNDP and advocacy with Government partners, by UNAIDS and WHO, PLHIV played a more significant role in the implementation of the GF NFM III, particularly related to activities for AGYW and those lead by PLHIV community cadres to reduce new infections and ensure greater continuity of treatment and care by mothers and adolescents newly infected with HIV. UNAIDS and WHO served as technical leads on the steering committee of the CSO GF principal recipient and led advocacy for accountability around community engagement—always questioning the role of PLHIV, AGYW, and KPs in service delivery to ensure that the GAS is achieved with communities.

Enhance the capacity of MoFA, GHS staff and other stakeholders in nutrition education.	
Enhance the capacity of stakeholders particular Agricultural Extension Agents(AEAs)  and selected vulnerable households in producing nutrient rich crops particularly Orange-fleshed Sweet Potatoes and other vegetables.
projects.outcome: Vulnerable populations have increased capacity to demand & use services to improve their health and nutrition status

projects.name: Support the implementation and monitoring of the Education Plus Initiative
projects.description: Collaborate with other members of JUTA and allies from the Government, Academia and Civil Society to discuss measures for monitoring and maximizing the impact of the Education plus initiative.Collaborate with the Ghana AIDS Commission for the conduct of regular meetings of the Coalition and the implementation of key action plans on HIV Prevention
projects.outcome: National & local institutions have strengthened capacity to monitor and scale up high quality HIV prevention, treatment and support services

projects.name: Enhance the capacity of young people especially women (including the Young Health Advocates- YHAG) in leadership and advocacy to champion initiatives on HIV prevention, Sexual Health, Rights and other areas of empowerment
projects.outcome: National & local institutions have strengthened capacity to monitor and scale up high quality HIV prevention, treatment and support services

projects.name: Review the draft 2020 HIV Stigma Index Report and provide inputs to the Consultants for the completion of the draft report and its dissemination
projects.description: Review the draft 2020 HIV Stigma Index Report and provide inputs to the Consultants for the completion of the draft report and its dissemination
projects.outcome: Key and marginalized populations are empowered to access quality HIV/AIDS services

projects.name: Strengthen the support system for SGBV prevention, survivors and resilience of vulnerable population through various strategies including policy reviews, media advocacy and shelters for victims
projects.description:
Strengthen support system for SGBV survivors through (DOVVSU and MoGCSP) the One Stop Centre, SGBV Support Center (crisis center) and Shelters 	
Strengthen Resilience of  vulnerable population through the provision dignity kits & essential items to women & girls in urban slums, as entry point to SGBV/SRHR education & service delivery	
Support media and advocacy activities using social influencers (traditional, religious and political constituencies, etc.) to sensitize the general public on COVID-19, SGBV and existing mitigation measures through traditional and social media;	
Support the review and update of national policy and frameworks including the NPPoA of the Domestic Violence Act,  National Gender Policy and SGBV emergency plan for the Ministry of Gender, Children and social protection	
Engage influencers from traditional, religious and political constituencies, etc. to sensitize the general public on COVID-19, SGBV and existing mitigation measures through traditional and social media
projects.outcome: Vulnerable groups are made fully aware of and have access to the social protection services available to them

projects.name: Support policymakers and MMDAs in the development of green recovery packages/plans and mobilize public and private finance for green recovery, with focus on women and youth.
projects.description: Support policymakers and MMDAs in the development green recovery packages/plans by developing different options using PAGE tools and mobilising public and private finance for green recovery.
projects.outcome: Key sectoral policies are coherent with environmental policies and considerations to support climate-resilient inclusive economic growth

projects.name: Strengthen the technical and operational capacities of Governance and Cultural Institutions for effective service delivery
projects.description:
Contribute towards an efficient transportation system that promotes Ghana's ports and corridors to enhance inclusiveness, stimulate socio-economic development and facilitate domestic and regional trade and integration.	
Build capacity of judges on the safety of journalists	
Support Peace and Governance platform/initiatives to promote inclusive dialogue and reviews on the Future of Governance in Ghana	
Build capacity of culture personnel, heritage institutions and support heritage sites for sustainable tourism	
Strengthen capacities at sub-national levels for improved implementation of green recovery plans	
Celebrate International Days related to Culture and Development	
Support Beyond the Return Initiative
projects.outcome: Governance institutions have better tools to improve effectiveness, transparency, equitability  and gender-sensitivity in implementing policies and programmes and guaranteeing the rights of  all
